description: AURORA is a high-fidelity Earth-observation simulation and analysis framework that connects satellite mission dynamics with environmental change detection. We use NASA-derived/modelled Earth data to examine how variables change across regions and time, quantify the magnitude and direction of those trends, and assess their statistical significance. The system combines orbital/access modelling, observation scheduling, environmental analysis, and reproducible computational experiments to identify where meaningful changes are occurring.
summary: AURORA-SR is an Earth-observation research project that develops and evaluates models for spectral reconstruction and drought analysis. Its main research combines climate history with land-surface observations to explore environmental change. NASA POWER is the primary climate source: daily corrected precipitation and mean, maximum, and minimum air temperature are processed into rolling climate features, then aligned with Sentinel-2 scenes. The following 30 days of rainfall define an exploratory rainfall-deficit drought target. Sentinel-2 contributes vegetation and moisture signals, while SpectralNetV10 reconstructs six Sentinel-2-style bands from RGB imagery. The website makes selected research outputs accessible and adds a bounded NASA POWER Trend Lab, where visitors compare annual climate trends across four Indian grid points. The site uses a precomputed record and does not run the full research or training pipeline live. AURORA-SR supports transparent, exploratory analysis while stating the limits of model outputs and proxy labels.
details:
Description of Project

AURORA-SR: Earth-Observation Research

NASA Space Apps 2026 Challenge Theme: Be An Earth System Trend Detective!

Team: ASTRO BADDIES

AURORA-SR is mostly a research and model development effort. Models for spectral reconstruction and drought research are developed and analyzed to evaluate how climate and land-surface indicators affect environmental changes. This website allows users to view some model outputs and figures and perform trend analysis. It doesn't represent the actual research or model training pipeline.

NASA POWER is a primary source of climate data for the drought investigation. The pipeline uses daily Agroclimatology records that contain the corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) and 2-metre mean, maximum, and minimum air temperature (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN). Based on these data seven-, 15-, 30-, 60-, and 90-day climate features are derived and matched with the Sentinel-2 scenes' observations. Precipitation for the next 30 days is used for the drought target construction. The meteorological history from NASA POWER based on NASA GMAO MERRA-2 and GEOS-IT is a primary weather context.

Sentinel-2 gives some information about the land-surface state by using the vegetation and moisture stats. In an independent model pipeline, SpectralNetV10 is trained to reconstruct six Sentinel-2-style bands (B02, B03, B04, B08, B11, B12) from RGB imagery. Training and evaluation of the model happens outside the static website.

Trend Lab shows regional analysis by using a bundle of annual series extracted from NASA POWER monthly data for 1981–2025 for four selected grid points in India. The user can choose one out of six climate variables, compare locations, select years, check change rate per decade and its uncertainty, and export annual values. The trend test checks the slope of each location against zero; it doesn't check if the slopes of different locations are significantly different. The website doesn't access any live data from NASA POWER or Sentinel-2 or train models in the browser.

AURORA-SR combines climate history, satellite-based surface state, spectral reconstruction, and drought models research into one single tool. Issues that need to be taken into account are the different time and spatial resolutions of the sources, data gaps because of clouds, autocorrelation, uncertainty, and proxy label issues.

From a methodological perspective, the research is done in Python using pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and PyTorch. Website development uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Climate data comes from NASA POWER Daily and Monthly Point APIs. Optional access to the Sentinel-2 scenes is available through Microsoft Planetary Computer.

Rainfall-deficit target is a proxy label, not a direct field assessment of drought, crop damage, or soil moisture condition. POWER grid cells are not local weather stations. Trend Lab includes four bundles of points, and statistical significance does not mean causality or effect.
